title: Gorsefield timekeeping rollout options
brief: I lead the timekeeping project at Gorsefield Hospital Trust, and the programme board will read this printed on 2026-11-09 to choose how we roll the new staff timekeeping system out to 900 staff on 24 wards. Under "The goal": every ward on the new system before the pay cut-off on 2027-03-26. Under "Rollout options", as a table with duration, extra cost and risk: A, switch all 24 wards on 2027-01-04 after 12 weeks of preparation, 40000 dollars of extra cover, risk that a fault hits every ward at once; B, ward by ward over 12 weeks from 2027-01-11, 2 wards per week, 95000 dollars of extra support staff, risk of running two systems for 12 weeks and double-entry errors; C, a pilot on 2 wards for 4 weeks from 2027-01-11, then the other 22 wards in two waves on 2027-02-15 and 2027-03-08, 70000 dollars, risk that the pilot wards are not typical. Under "If it goes wrong", what would have to be undone: A, go back to paper for all 900 staff, which needs 3 days and about 60 managers; B, revert only the wards switched so far, a ward at a time; C, stop after the pilot with only 2 wards to revert. Under "Recommendation": C, because it fits before the cut-off and limits the worst case to 2 wards. Make the recommendation and the cut-off date impossible to miss.

edit.request: Option C's extra cost is now 65000 dollars and its second wave moves to 2027-03-01.
